Today's 9to5Toys lunch deal report leads with Apple's official refurbished store offering up to $300 off the most affordable 2026 Studio Display, alongside the ongoing Amazon Early Fall Prime Day sale and an all-time low price on a single AirTag 2. While the $500 discount on the M5 Pro MacBook Pro may be the best deal of this Early Fall Prime Day, Belkin's holiday deals have already kicked off starting at $13, with its new 25W MagSafe charger hitting a new low; Eve's official Early Fall Prime Day deals have also launched with up to 38% off, including Matter/HomeKit switches, outlets, and power strips starting at $30. Today also brings an extra 10% off (already discounted) on official Apple USB-C, Thunderbolt, and MagSafe cables, starting at $7.50 each. See below for details.

You can still grab a single 2026 AirTag 2 at an all-time low on Amazon.

We've caught the 4-pack deal several times, but if you don't need four, Amazon's Early Fall Prime Day mega sale is still offering brand-new 2026 AirTag 2 units at the lowest price ever.

Though the discount isn't huge, Prime members get free shipping at $24, but note this is a 2026 Apple product that already launched at just $29.

  • AirTag 2 $24 (regular price $29) — matching the all-time low

The 4-pack is still on sale at $89, or $22.50 each. However, we've seen it drop by $9 multiple times over the past two months, and the same could happen again during Early Fall Prime Day.

That also suggests the single pack could drop further, but by how much?

Sure, $20 with Prime free shipping would be tempting, and it's not impossible right now, but there's no way to know, and it would only be $4 less than the current price. Looking at past major sales where AirTags hit $20 or below, unless you're ready to pounce instantly, actually getting one at that price may be harder than you'd think.

Before Early Fall Prime Day ends at midnight ET on October 8, the single pack could indeed drop slightly more, but a much steeper drop is unlikely.

Most affordable 2026 Studio Display sees up to $300 off at Apple's official refurbished store today

Alongside the ongoing Amazon Early Fall Prime Day mega sale, Apple's certified refurbished store is also offering attractive deals on the most affordable 2026 Apple Studio Display: $240 off the tilt-adjustable stand version, and $300 off the tilt- and height-adjustable stand version.

Apple's official refurbished store is once again offering the 2026 Apple Studio Display with tilt-adjustable stand for $1,359 with free shipping. That model retails for $1,599, now $240 off; Amazon currently sells it for $1,550 and has never dropped below $1,484.

As for the 2026 model with tilt- and height-adjustable stand, it's $1,699 with free shipping. That model retails for $1,999, now a hefty $300 off—well below Amazon's current $1,984; the model has never sold for less than $1,886 new on Amazon.

Here's what you need to know about Apple Refurbished Store products:

  • Undergo rigorous refurbishment process before sale
  • Backed by Apple's one-year limited warranty
  • Covered by Apple's 14-day return policy
  • AppleCare available for purchase
  • Engraving and gift wrapping not available
  • Limited stock available

$500 off the M5 Pro MacBook Pro may be the best deal of this Early Fall Prime Day

Amazon's Early Fall Prime Day mega sale is in full swing with thousands of items discounted, but among the many Apple deals we're featuring, one stands out—grab it before it's gone. While next week's Prime Day pricing on the latest MacBook Pro lineup is hard to predict, you can already snag this M5 Pro 2TB model with up to $500 off.

Amazon currently offers the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro in Space Gray and Silver, with 24GB RAM, 2TB storage, and upgraded 18-core CPU/20-core GPU specs, for $2,699 with free shipping.

Still a significant investment, but this is the model with Apple's M5 Pro chip, upgraded 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU, and 2TB storage—priced the same as the lower-tier 15/16-core model.

Originally $3,199, you can now get it for $500 below retail.

Official Apple USB-C, Thunderbolt, and MagSafe cables get an extra 10% off (already discounted), starting at $7.50 each today

Ongoing deal: Beats' all-new 360 ANC headphones launch deal — modular Cushion Kit 80% off at $10

Quick update: Yesterday Amazon had a countdown clock for the Beats all-new 360 ANC headphones launch deal, but it looks like Amazon decided to extend the 80% discount on the modular Cushion Kit through today.

As previously reported, the all-new Beats 360 features a modular design where users can flip off the ear cushions and headband pads to customize the look and feel, with Performance Knit and UltraPlush options:

  • Beats 360 Over-Ear Headphones $350
  • Beats 360 Cushion Kit $10 (regular price $50)

The headphones are selling at regular price, but the Cushion Kit is still 80% off on Amazon. The deal was set to end yesterday, but it's still live this morning.

Pitaka aerospace-grade aramid fiber iPhone Duo case doesn't need to be bought at retail—Amazon has it at half price today

Apple's all-new iPhone Duo is about to go on sale, and accessories to enhance the experience are rolling out. While the USB-C Apple Pencil may be the most powerful Duo accessory for some users, we've also spotted an early bird deal on the Pitaka iPhone Duo Edge Case—retail price $100, now $49.99 with free shipping on Amazon.

While this aerospace-grade aramid fiber Pitaka iPhone Duo Edge Case has never sold for $100 on Amazon, the official site does list it at that price. Multiple colors are now available for $50. The product originally launched on Amazon at $60, so the actual discount is only $10, but of course, don't get "tricked" into paying $100.

  • Pitaka iPhone Duo Edge Case $50 (Amazon was $60, retail $100)

After rolling out multiple Early Fall Prime Day deals, Twelve South is set to officially unveil the all-new Airfly Drive today. As the latest addition to the Airfly lineup, this new CarPlay and Android Auto adapter is now available for $39.99. The market is flooded with knockoff brands making similar products (usually with rougher designs), but Twelve South has finally entered the scene.

Click here for more details.
